rows.title: Divide whole numbers and keep a remainder
rows.gap: Integer division, remainder and explicit Double conversion; explain bounds without executing overflow.
rows.assessment: Positive/negative and exact/non-exact division; zero divisor and Int.min/-1 rejected before arithmetic by a safe function.
rows.authoringBoundary: Check a zero divisor and Int.min with divisor -1 before either division or remainder; never execute the overflowing boundary as a demo.

rows.title: Return named parts in a tuple
rows.gap: Tuple fields, positional/named access and destructuring, beyond incidental enumerated pairs.
rows.assessment: Two inputs change both named results.

rows.title: Repeat until a condition changes
rows.gap: while versus repeat-while initial-condition behavior.
rows.assessment: Initially false and several-iteration cases terminate.

rows.title: Skip an item or stop a loop
rows.gap: continue versus break in a bounded sequence.
rows.assessment: Skipped item, early stop, empty input.

rows.title: Unwrap an optional with if let
rows.gap: Present/absent/empty String are distinct; full binding block rather than prior inline mention.
rows.assessment: All three branches with changed values.

rows.title: Leave early with guard let
rows.gap: Failable Int parsing and guard-bound value scope.
rows.assessment: Malformed, valid and out-of-range application inputs.

rows.title: Follow an optional chain
rows.gap: Chained property/method access yields an optional; no forced unwrap.
rows.assessment: Missing outer and inner values plus present result.

rows.title: Count characters rather than bytes
rows.gap: Character iteration and UTF-8 count differ; no integer string subscripting.
rows.assessment: ASCII, combined accent and emoji examples.

rows.title: Use String indices and own a substring
rows.gap: Safe index movement and Substring-to-String ownership boundary.
rows.assessment: Empty/short/multicharacter input, no invalid index executed.

rows.title: Read array positions and slices safely
rows.gap: indices/first and slice index preservation, explicit Array conversion.
rows.assessment: Empty input, valid bounds and nonzero slice start.

rows.title: Look up, update and remove dictionary entries
rows.gap: Optional lookup versus default read, replacement/removal and deterministic display.
rows.assessment: Missing key, existing value and source state.

rows.title: Combine sets by membership
rows.gap: Union/intersection/subtraction with ordered display only for comparison.
rows.assessment: Overlap, disjoint and repeated source items.

rows.title: Collect variadic function arguments
rows.gap: Variadic parameter becomes an array; distinguish existing defaults.
rows.assessment: Zero, one and multiple values.

rows.title: Modify a caller value with inout
rows.gap: Ampersand call, mutation and exclusive access; no unsafe alias execution.
rows.assessment: Changed caller value, negative compile fixture for conflicting access.

rows.title: Pass and return a function value
rows.gap: Explicit function type and returned closure capture, beyond collection callback syntax.
rows.assessment: Two supplied operations and independent captured values.
rows.authoringBoundary: Separate closure-factory calls own independent captured state; assigning one closure to another name is not another factory call.

rows.title: Store an escaping closure
rows.gap: Escaping lifetime and explicit capture behavior; reuse existing ARC lesson instead of duplicating cycles.
rows.assessment: Stored callback after registration; compile rejection without required escaping annotation.

rows.title: Mutate a struct without sharing its value
rows.gap: mutating methods and independent copied value.
rows.assessment: Original/copy divergence and let-mutation compile rejection.
rows.authoringBoundary: Demonstrate a struct with value-only stored fields. A struct containing a class reference does not recursively deep-copy that object.

rows.title: Validate construction with a failable initializer
rows.gap: init? rejects invalid construction, distinct from a later observer.
rows.assessment: Lower/upper boundary and valid construction.

rows.title: Translate through a computed setter
rows.gap: get/set and newValue map to stored state.
rows.assessment: Read/write roundtrip and changed source state.

rows.title: Keep type-wide members separate from instances
rows.gap: static constants/functions accessed on a type, not accidental shared mutable globals.
rows.assessment: Two independent instances and type function.

rows.title: Override inherited behavior
rows.gap: Superclass, override and super, with dynamic dispatch.
rows.assessment: Base and subclass outputs; missing override compile rejection.

rows.title: Check and safely downcast a value
rows.gap: is and as? on heterogeneous class values; no forced cast.
rows.assessment: Matching and nonmatching concrete types.

rows.title: Convert enum raw values safely
rows.gap: Raw value versus associated value and failable rawValue initializer.
rows.assessment: Known and unknown raw inputs.

rows.title: Give values equality and hashing contracts
rows.gap: Synthesized Equatable/Hashable from stored values; never assert randomized numeric hash output.
rows.assessment: Equal values deduplicate; differing field remains distinct.

rows.title: Provide a default protocol requirement
rows.gap: Required method and default implementation, with explicit conformer override.
rows.assessment: Two conformers through protocol use; avoid misleading nonrequirement dispatch.

rows.title: Constrain a generic operation
rows.gap: Protocol constraints and where relationships rather than unconstrained T.
rows.assessment: Multiple admissible types and intended nonconforming compile rejection.
rows.authoringBoundary: Keep simple protocol constraints and where spelling; cross-conformer associated-type equality belongs in48.

rows.title: Connect protocol associated types
rows.gap: associatedtype and a generic equality relationship between conformers.
rows.assessment: Matching element types accepted, mismatched relationship rejected.
rows.authoringBoundary: Teach the associated-type equality relation explicitly, rather than making47 a prerequisite for unexplained syntax.

rows.title: Distinguish opaque and boxed protocol values
rows.gap: some preserves one hidden concrete identity; any stores conforming alternatives.
rows.assessment: Stable opaque result accepted, incompatible result branches rejected.
rows.authoringBoundary: Limit the one-hidden-concrete-type explanation to opaque results; some parameter syntax has a distinct generic-shorthand role and is not this lesson.

rows.title: Keep only successful optional transformations
rows.gap: compactMap removes nil results, not arbitrary false-like values.
rows.assessment: Valid zero, malformed text and empty source.

rows.title: Accumulate a collection into one result
rows.gap: reduce initial accumulator and closure input/result.
rows.assessment: Empty input and changed initial accumulator.

rows.title: Store success or failure as a Result
rows.gap: Result value and switch versus immediate throwing; no claim it runs asynchronously.
rows.assessment: Success and typed failure consumption.

rows.title: Join fixed child tasks with async let
rows.gap: Structured child lifetimes and awaiting results; no promised speed or scheduling order.
rows.assessment: Both results consumed, propagated failure and bounded cleanup evidence.

rows.title: Collect a dynamic task group
rows.gap: Add child tasks and consume completion results; normalize order when order is irrelevant.
rows.assessment: Empty/multiple jobs and exact result multiplicity; cooperative cancellation only.

rows.title: Draw an access boundary between modules
rows.gap: public versus internal/private across two actually compiled modules.
rows.assessment: Allowed exported API and intended hidden-symbol compile rejection.
rows.authoringBoundary: A public type does not automatically make its members or initializer public; demonstrate the actual exported boundary.

rows.title: Build a small local Swift package
rows.gap: Manifest, library/executable targets and an intra-package target dependency; no registry installation.
rows.assessment: Actual offline build/run with complete files.
rows.authoringBoundary: One offline package with a library target and executable target depending on it. No second package, registry resolution or external dependency is required.

rows.title: Discover and run Swift tests
rows.gap: Swift Testing assertions, discovery and useful failing diagnostics.
rows.assessment: Passing suite, deliberate assertion failure and zero-tests distinction.

rows.title: Diagnose a compile error and a logic error
rows.gap: Minimal reproduction and expected-versus-actual tracing, not arbitrary debugger/tool installation.
rows.assessment: Specific compile diagnostic then corrected source; changed input catches logic bug.

limits: No Swift browser compiler exists in this app. Current user Run uses an explicitly connected Mac companion.
Linux native evidence does not establish Apple SwiftUI UI behavior, macOS sandbox execution or Xcode SDK compatibility.
Existing companion does not explicitly select language mode 6; compiler version alone is not strict-concurrency proof. Treat a mode change as a separately reviewed runtime delta.
Three new module/package/testing workflows are local multifile companions, not single-file Mac Run claims.
SwiftUI09 remains an optional Apple-platform application; Stanford CS193p is an optional continuation benchmark, not core language equivalence.
exclusions: Full SwiftUI/SwiftData/UIKit application course, gestures, animation and Apple persistence frameworks.
Unsafe pointers, C interoperability, custom operators, macros, noncopyable ownership, parameter packs and ABI engineering.
Custom property wrappers/result builders and advanced custom subscripts: documented specialization; existing SwiftUI wrapper use remains explained locally.
Network services, package registries and external dependencies.
Sorting/data-science/graphics additions merely to match another track count.
existingCorrections: Replace outdated compiler-unavailable notes with precise native-versus-Mac-versus-Apple boundaries.
Correct swift11 catalog restart claim to actual within-run disk roundtrip unless a separate restart companion is authored and tested.
Correct swift09 project form wording to existing form controls in VStack, retain manual Apple UI checks.
Explicit prerequisite DAG and cross-level Study navigation; retain all IDs and existing applications.
Add targeted changed-input behavior checks where existing contracts are underassessed; exact deltas reviewed before integration.
Readably format any repaired complete block and rerun exact source. Do not add repeated internal runtime-policy paragraphs.
